title: Sequential Multi-Review Routing and Frozen Handoff
objective: Falsify discretionary routing, mutable handoff, and proposer-side contamination in the sequential multi-review topology before treating manual reviewer behavior as governance enforcement.
invariants: High-risk or promotion-authoritative transitions always route to R3 after R2 regardless of R2 disposition.
Lower-risk R3 routing is determined only by frozen policy inputs, never post-hoc preference.
R1-middle cannot modify the original review request, candidate/base identity, evidence manifest hash, or corpus hash.
R1-middle freezes the complete raw R2 result and hashes it.
Any normalized R2 summary is deterministic and cannot silently omit material R2 fields.
R1-middle adds no independent conclusion or promotion recommendation.
R3 receives the same frozen original evidence identity plus the frozen R2 result/summary identity.
Shared conversational memory is not part of L10 authority; memory contamination is isolated to L11.
tests: L10-01 high-risk PASS still requires R3
L10-02 high-risk FAIL still requires R3
L10-03 policy-required dual review routes R3
L10-04 low-risk no-trigger path may stop after R2
L10-05 normalized R2 handoff is byte-deterministic
L10-06 all raw R2 material fields survive normalization
L10-07 mutated frozen packet is rejected
L10-09 R1-middle opinion field is forbidden
L10-10 changed policy inputs require a new routing decision identity
failure_rule: Any discretionary high-risk bypass, packet mutation, omitted R2 material field, unbound handoff identity, or R1-middle opinion injection is a mechanism failure.
pass_scope: A deterministic pass qualifies only the prototype routing/handoff mechanism under these tests. It does not qualify reviewer semantics, shared-memory isolation, external provider behavior, or PR11 promotion.
